pillar_reactions.evidence: Pushed back on the substance of the mobility half: 'I know flexibility is one of my weakest points and my wife hates that I don't do yoga, but I feel that being tighter like helps me, I don't know why. I feel like the people that stretch are the ones that get injured more, and if I don't stretch I haven't been getting injured.' The rep corrected him with a flexibility-versus-mobility distinction — 'mobility is building strength that protects the joints... you can be flexible and not mobile' — and he accepted it, but he had also already questioned whether Trevor's morning flow work is realistic 'for a normal dad'. The kettlebell half drew no resistance at all; he has wanted to do it for two years.

This was the centre of gravity of the call and he interrogated it for the best part of thirty minutes — dairy, minerals and vitamins, pre-workout carbohydrate, fasting protocols, whether the approach is 'very Whole30-ish', and finally whether it could address his psoriasis. Every question was constructive and he repeatedly signalled alignment ('It's a full balance', 'That sounds so sustainable'). The one thing he was sold that he had not previously believed is that a weekly life day is compatible with results.

Needed the delivery model explained three separate times. He asked what the weekly call is, was told it is a check-in and not a call; asked how progression from a 16 kg to an 18 kg bell is communicated — 'is there like a pop-up, hey, you've progressed to the 18s?'; was told 'No, it's all with Trevor', answered 'Kind of. So it's not like, so how can I explain this?', and needed the app-versus-coach distinction re-explained with a Zoom analogy before it landed. He also had to ask twice to confirm there is only one call with Trevor ever. The pillar he most needed — he has no plan and cannot retain flows — is the one he understood least.

anchors.raw: I guess in my mind, I didn't know what I was expecting, but I was thinking like a $500 a month kind of a deal.
anchors.note: He arrived with $500 a month in his head against $1,000 a month effective, and said so only at minute 58 after the refusal. Notably he paired it with an explicit value affirmation — 'I don't want to shortchange Trevor and your system at all' — so the gap was affordability against expectation, not a disputed valuation.

anchors.raw: I have more on my credit card than I do on my bank account, and I have maybe six grand in my bank account, and that's got to cover bills and trying to switch rent and doing this and that... I have to move out of my house. I have to sell my house.
anchors.note: The dominant anchor. Every dollar he has is spoken for by a divorce in progress, and the six thousand in his account is almost exactly the price of the programme and entirely committed elsewhere. He identified the resolution himself — 'once I sell my house, it's on' — which is the honest follow-up date nobody booked.

anchors.raw: I'd say probably 70% of our clients are business owners. Uh, don't worry. We'll help you write it off... I signed up a guy yesterday and we've framed the invoice as, let me tell you exactly what it was framed as, safety and injury prevention program.
anchors.note: The sixth appearance of this lever in the batch and by far the most concrete — a named invoice description, a specific client from the previous day and a stated willingness to reissue documentation. Deployed within seconds of the price landing. The prospect engaged with it directly, repeating the phrase back: 'Safety and Injury Prevention Protocol. What is it?'

anchors.raw: I resort to going back to his reels, looking at it, watching it, and then doing a set of whatever that is... there's Arian on Instagram, the war horse guy, he's got his own methods and stuff
anchors.competitor: Trevor's own free reels and other kettlebell creators
anchors.note: Two years of consuming the free version is what brought him here, and it is also his fallback. Unusually, the free content is the source of his stated pain rather than a satisfying substitute — the friction of hunting reels mid-workout is the problem the offer solves — which makes this an anchor the rep could have converted and largely did.

anchors.raw: I'm already paying for the gym, I like going there, the sauna, it's just like a spa kind of deal
anchors.note: He already pays for a facility he enjoys and intends to keep using, so the programme is additive spend rather than a substitution. The rep noted Trevor 'talks down about the gym in his videos' without resolving the tension.

unmet_demand.want: Dietary management of psoriasis as an alternative to dermatologist-prescribed injections
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep conceded the expertise gap directly — 'I don't think Trevor's like an expert on psoriasis. So it's not gonna be like, oh, you've got psoriasis, just cut this out' — while still agreeing to run elimination trials. The programme cannot deliver what the prospect is hoping for, and nobody redirected him to the clinician who could.

unmet_demand.want: Objective baseline and progress measurement — body composition testing and blood work, which competitors apparently include
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Explicitly not offered and actively downplayed: 'We don't do that... I don't think they're that accurate... the body fat stuff, tracking that side of things, it's not really that important' and 'I've never had my blood work checked either. It's not something that's super necessary.' The prospect raised it because 'there's other programs where when you join, they get you the body fat test thing', so this is a live competitive gap as well as a clinical one for a man with an unmanaged autoimmune condition.

unmet_demand.want: A solution to the energy collapse mid-workout — the single problem he says stands between him and success
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme almost certainly addresses it through the nutrition pillar, and the rep even described his own pre-training meal, but it was never framed as the answer to the thing the prospect had named twice. He restated it unresolved at minute 59: 'If I could figure out the energy component, I know I could be successful.'
